_meta.indication: VIVJOA is an azole antifungal indicated to reduce the incidence of recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis (RVVC) in females with a history of RVVC who are NOT of reproductive potential.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled trial with an open-label induction phase (three sequential doses of fluconazole 150 mg every 72 hours on Days 1, 4 and 7) and an 11-week maintenance phase; patients randomized 2:1 to VIVJOA 150 mg or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults and post-menarchal pediatric females with a history of RVVC (>=3 episodes of VVC in a 12-month period).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients with >=1 culture-verified acute VVC episode during the Maintenance Phase through Week 48.
pivotal_trials.n: Trial 1 maintenance phase: 326 randomized (217 VIVJOA, 109 placebo).
pivotal_trials.result: Proportion of patients with >=1 culture-verified acute VVC episode through Week 48: 6.7% VIVJOA vs 42.8% placebo (p<0.001).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled trial with an open-label induction phase and an 11-week maintenance phase; patients randomized 2:1 to VIVJOA 150 mg or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults and post-menarchal pediatric females with a history of RVVC (>=3 episodes of VVC in a 12-month period).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients with >=1 culture-verified acute VVC episode during the Maintenance Phase through Week 48.
pivotal_trials.n: Trial 2 maintenance phase: 330 randomized (220 VIVJOA, 110 placebo).
pivotal_trials.result: Proportion of patients with >=1 culture-verified acute VVC episode through Week 48: 3.9% VIVJOA vs 39.4% placebo (p<0.001).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind trial evaluating VIVJOA versus fluconazole and placebo, with induction and maintenance phases; patients randomized 2:1 to VIVJOA or fluconazole/placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults and post-menarchal pediatric females with RVVC; conducted entirely in the United States.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients with >=1 culture-verified acute VVC episode during the maintenance phase (through Week 50) or who failed clearing their infection during the induction phase.
pivotal_trials.result: Proportion of patients with >=1 culture-verified acute VVC episode through Week 50 or unresolved episode during induction: 10.3% VIVJOA vs 42.9% fluconazole/placebo (p<0.001).

key_safety: Most frequently reported adverse reactions (incidence >2%) were headache (7.4%) and nausea (3.6%). One of 580 (0.2%) VIVJOA-treated patients discontinued due to an adverse reaction (allergic dermatitis).
target_moa: Oteseconazole is an azole antifungal that inhibits fungal lanosterol demethylase (CYP51 / sterol 14-alpha demethylase), blocking conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol required for fungal cell membrane formation.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee was not convened for this NDA.
